newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr rises vs yen by noon Tokyo, focus on mark/yen.
newsitem.headline: Dlr rises vs yen by noon Tokyo, focus on mark/yen.

text.p: 0300 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0300 GMT
The dollar crept higher versus the yen by noon Tokyo on Wednesday, but a lack of fresh dollar/yen moving news kept operators focused on mark/yen.
"Dollar/yen edged higher as dollar buying by Japanese importers outweighed offers," said a trader at a city bank.
Investment trusts and interbank players were also among dollar buyers this morning, traders said.
Buy-backs in mark/yen after a sharp overnight fall also gave indirect support to dollar/yen, although sporadic mark/yen selling by Japanese exporters was detected, traders said.
The German currency was quoted at around 63.38/41 yen as of 0320 GMT, off its earlier high of around 63.50 yen.
The mark closed at 63.05 yen in New York on Tuesday, down sharply from around 64.46 yen in late Tokyo on Tuesday.
Traders were puzzled by dollar/yen's sharp overnight dip.
"A dip in mark/yen alone is not enough to explain why dollar/yen also had to fall so sharply overnight," said the city bank trader.
"A lot of people had been looking for a test of 117 yen. After the overnight fall, however, people have become more cautious about setting up dollar/yen longs," said a trader at another city bank.
Traders said dollar/yen's direction in the afternoon likely to dictated by mark/yen's moves.
"If the mark falls back against the yen, say below 63 yen, then dollar/yen is also likely to head lower," said a trust bank trader.
"However, if mark/yen settles down around current levels, we could see more upside room for dollar/yen," he added.
Traders expect the German currency to continue facing selling pressure due to a growing perception that Europe's planned single currency 'euro' will be broad-based and weak.

"Buba officials so far have failed to show strong determination to stop the mark's fall. Some players suspect that Buba might be willing to tolerate the dollar/mark's rise to around 1.85 marks," said a trader at another city bank.

Worries about a weak euro were exacerbated after Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Koebnick told German radio on Tuesday that the euro could be stable even if Germany and France missed the targets, traders said.
The dollar was off its earlier lows versus the mark in Tokyo, but remained within a relatively narrow range.
The dollar surged to its highest level against the mark in almost six years in Tuesday's New York session, buoyed by remarks from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.

In his semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony, Greenspan told a House Banking subcommittee on Tuesday that U.S. economic growth appeared to be slowing and that he was confident of modest inflation through the end of 1997.
The dollar closed at 114.95/00 yen and 1.8230/40 marks in New York on Tuesday. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780
